neighbours.label: the words 'thermodynamics' and 'entropy' (and close forms such as 'thermodynamic'), in any sentence; the same physics described without those words (heat flow, engine efficiency) stays low
fire: Every chemistry student learns the first law of thermodynamics.
The room's entropy rose as the ice melted.
Black holes have an entropy proportional to their area.
She wrote her thesis on the thermodynamics of proteins.
A thermodynamic cycle returns the gas to its starting state.
Shannon borrowed the word entropy for information theory.
Living things keep their entropy low by eating.
quiet: Every chemistry student learns how heat flows from hot to cold.
The room grew messier as the party went on.
Black holes have a surface area that grows as they eat stars.
She wrote her thesis on the folding of proteins.
A full cycle returns the gas to its starting pressure and volume.
Shannon borrowed the word bit for information theory.
The lecture covered statistical mechanics of springs.
Living things keep warm by eating.
neighbours.notes: Survivor of a category census (50 items x 8 passage pairs, census, fresh-sentence triage, probes). An early-layer (L4) word unit. Triage: 'the second law of thermodynamics' 1.28, 'entropy in a closed system' 0.44; the thermostat 0.01, Newton's laws 0.004. Probes: 'Boltzmann linked entropy to probability' 0.50, 'Entropy measures disorder' 0.25 (sentence-initial); the thermos 0.15; heat flowing from hot to cold 0.01, engine efficiency 0.01, the refrigerator 0.01.
